There’s a duck on Alligator’s lawn, and Alligator isn’t happy about it. Worse, when Alligator tries to get Duck to go away, the bird says they’re nobody’s duck. But how can that be? Surely, this is someone’s duck. Starting to grow impatient, Alligator sets off to find whoever is responsible for this quacky individual.

From the library to theater, to the race track, to a leap from an airplane, Alligator and Duck search all over town. Will they ever find out whose duck this is? And will some of Duck’s sunny attitude rub off on Alligator along the way? Whatever happens, one thing is sure: This duck knows how to have a good time.

This year’s race will be a relay, which means all the runners must compete in teams—and Steve’s teammates are the slowest in the forest.

Is Steve about to lose his first Race-a-thon ever? Come along as Steve prepares his team to handle rain, brambles, flooding, and more. By the time he’s done, the only runner who will be able to defeat Team Steve might be Steve himself.

Spork sticks out. In his kitchen, utensils have a single purpose. Even though he tries to act more spoonish or look more forkish, he never gets picked at mealtime. Instead, he sits and watches while the forks twirl knots of noodles and the spoons scoop up mountains of peas. They even get to enjoy a bubbly bath in the sink when dinner is over.

He seems destined for a life in the drawer … until one day, a messy guest arrives. This guest doesn’t seem to care about cutlery customs. Spork wonders—could this be his chance to find his way to the table? Could his uniqueness make him the best solution for this problem?

A metaphor-rich celebration of hybrid identities, Spork is a “multi-cutlery” tale for anyone who’s ever felt like a misfit. Exploring themes of purpose, conformity, diversity, and finding your place in the world, Spork is written by Kyo Maclear and illustrated by Isabelle Arsenault. Published by Kids Can Press.

Spork sticks out. In his kitchen, utensils have a single purpose. Even though he tries to act more spoonish or look more forkish, he never gets picked at mealtime. Instead, he sits and watches while the forks twirl knots of noodles and the spoons scoop up mountains of peas. They even get to enjoy a bubbly bath in the sink when dinner is over.

He seems destined for a life in the drawer … until one day, a messy guest arrives. This guest doesn’t seem to care about cutlery customs. Spork wonders—could this be his chance to find his way to the table? Could his uniqueness make him the best solution for this problem?

A metaphor-rich celebration of hybrid identities, Spork is a “multi-cutlery” tale for anyone who’s ever felt like a misfit. Exploring themes of purpose, conformity, diversity, and finding your place in the world, Spork is written by Kyo Maclear and illustrated by Isabelle Arsenault. Published by Kids Can Press.

Today, Hiku feels grumpy. The ice is too bright, the sun is too hot, and his mummy woke him up too early. Then Hiku remembers his whole family is coming for a visit—which is the last thing he wants right now. He doesn’t feel like smiling, being polite, and getting teased by his aunts, uncles, nephews, nieces, and cousins. He wants to be alone.

But when Hiku sneaks off to his special snow hole, he starts to think about all the fun times he’s had with his family. Will Hiku realize he’s missing out on having fun and making memories? And if he does, will he make it back in time for the family photo? Come along with Hiku and find out!

Hiku is a story about how, with a little space and time to think, even grumpy days can get better. The narrative shows that feeling unhappy can be normal, and that it’s okay to take time for oneself when you’re not feeling up to socializing. Written by Nicole Snitselaar, illustrated by Coralie Saudo, and published by Top That! Publishing.

Today, Hiku feels grumpy. The ice is too bright, the sun is too hot, and his mummy woke him up too early. Then Hiku remembers his whole family is coming for a visit—which is the last thing he wants right now. He doesn’t feel like smiling, being polite, and getting teased by his aunts, uncles, nephews, nieces, and cousins. He wants to be alone.

But when Hiku sneaks off to his special snow hole, he starts to think about all the fun times he’s had with his family. Will Hiku realize he’s missing out on having fun and making memories? And if he does, will he make it back in time for the family photo? Come along with Hiku and find out!

Hiku is a story about how, with a little space and time to think, even grumpy days can get better. The narrative shows that feeling unhappy can be normal, and that it’s okay to take time for oneself when you’re not feeling up to socializing. Written by Nicole Snitselaar, illustrated by Coralie Saudo, and published by Top That! Publishing.

"The most certain way to succeed is always to try just one more time." -Thomas Edison
From the curiosity of Leonardo da Vinci to the dedication of Marie Curie, Inventors Who Changed the World is a young child's first introduction to the brilliant people who taught us the meaning of perseverance and innovation. Simple text and adorable illustrations tell the contributions of nine renowned inventors from around the world: Cai Lun, Leonardo da Vinci, Marie Curie, Thomas Edison, Orville and Wilbur Wright, Grace Hopper, Johannes Gutenberg, and Louis Pasteur. Inspire your own little inventor with the words of these inventive heroes who changed the world.
Inventors Who Changed the World is written by Heidi Poelman, illustrated by Kyle Kershner and published by Familius.

Vooks brings children’s storybooks to life through animation. With an expansive library of titles, the Vooks storybooks experience feature animation, sound, and narration to classic and award-winning books that are loved by parents and educators alike. Our kid-safe and ad-free streaming library of read-aloud animated storybooks transforms reading by bringing words to life in order to spark every child's imagination. Vooks combines the love, trust, and safety of children’s books with the convenience of online streaming, for a whole new way to experience stories.

Dandelions are a flowering weed—but they’re also much more than that. After they flower, each dandelion turns into a fluffy ball of puffy seeds. And then, with a poof, the seeds scatter. Drifting on the wind, tucked in a tuft of fur, carried on a shoe, even traveling through something’s belly. The seeds disperse, hitching rides to spread far and wide.

Is there any place on earth where a dandelion can’t make a home? Follow these cheery blossoms as they spring up, spread out, and fly off on the wind like a wish. You might be surprised at just how far such tiny things can wander.

Surprisingly resilient and adaptable—not unlike humans—Little Dandelion Seeds the World shows how dandelions are able to thrive on all seven continents. The story introduces diverse people groups, animals, and habitats as it follows dandelions around the globe. Written by Julia Richardson, illustrated by Kristen and Kevin Howdeshell, and published by Sleeping Bear Press.

Dandelions are a flowering weed—but they’re also much more than that. After they flower, each dandelion turns into a fluffy ball of puffy seeds. And then, with a poof, the seeds scatter. Drifting on the wind, tucked in a tuft of fur, carried on a shoe, even traveling through something’s belly. The seeds disperse, hitching rides to spread far and wide.

Is there any place on earth where a dandelion can’t make a home? Follow these cheery blossoms as they spring up, spread out, and fly off on the wind like a wish. You might be surprised at just how far such tiny things can wander.

Surprisingly resilient and adaptable—not unlike humans—Little Dandelion Seeds the World shows how dandelions are able to thrive on all seven continents. The story introduces diverse people groups, animals, and habitats as it follows dandelions around the globe. Written by Julia Richardson, illustrated by Kristen and Kevin Howdeshell, and published by Sleeping Bear Press.

Up in the garden, a girl stands and plans. Her hands are full of seeds and her head is full of dreams. But before she and Nana can get started on tending their garden—leaves and sprouts, growing vegetables, and ripening fruit—they have to wait. Down in the dirt, things need to warm up and dry out. There’s a busy world under their feet, full of earthworms, pillbugs, and more.

Planning, planting, and harvesting will take all year. But there are two sides to the story—what happens above, and what happens below. Come meet the incredible creatures who make our gardens their home, bring the world to life, and help the greenery around us grow.

A story of patience, care, and coexistence, Up in the Garden and Down in the Dirt shows us the cycle of our seasons. It also introduces us to a cast of insects and animals who make our world vibrant and green. Written by Kate Messner, illustrated by Christopher Silas Neal, and published by Chronicle Books.

Up in the garden, a girl stands and plans. Her hands are full of seeds and her head is full of dreams. But before she and Nana can get started on tending their garden—leaves and sprouts, growing vegetables, and ripening fruit—they have to wait. Down in the dirt, things need to warm up and dry out. There’s a busy world under their feet, full of earthworms, pillbugs, and more.

Planning, planting, and harvesting will take all year. But there are two sides to the story—what happens above, and what happens below. Come meet the incredible creatures who make our gardens their home, bring the world to life, and help the greenery around us grow.

A story of patience, care, and coexistence, Up in the Garden and Down in the Dirt shows us the cycle of our seasons. It also introduces us to a cast of insects and animals who make our world vibrant and green. Written by Kate Messner, illustrated by Christopher Silas Neal, and published by Chronicle Books.

Simon is a backstage cat. His owner is a celebrity. Together, they ride to the theater in a big, silver-grey limousine. Simon watches in the dressing room while his owner puts on rouge and powder. Then come eyelashes, lipstick, bracelets. Finally, a wig, shoes, and her costume. Then, it’s time for the show! Simon’s owner promises to come back and see him during intermission.

But then Simon sees a mouse, and he can’t help but chase it out of the dressing room. But what will happen when a falling prop spooks him onstage? This backstage cat is about to get an unexpected moment in the spotlight. It could be a disaster—or maybe it’ll turn Simon into a celebrity as well.

With a theater-themed vocabulary and mixed-media illustrations, Backstage Cat follows the silly misadventure of a rather mischievous kitty. Written by Harriet Ziefert, illustrated by Jenni Desmond, and published by Blue Apple Books.

Which mammal has three kinds of teeth that are all about the same height? Here’s a hint: You’re one of them! Humans have incisors, canines, and molars. Some animals have larger teeth than ours. Animals with large incisors eat plants, chewing up hard nuts and seeds. Long canines are for eating meat—and tall molars are for grinding up grass and other leafy plants.
What kind of animals have two incisors that grow out of their mouth, pointing up at the sky? And which mammal has canine teeth that stretch down toward their belly? Come along for the story of how our mouths evolved with the foods we eat, one pair of teeth at a time.

Which mammal has three kinds of teeth that are all about the same height? Here’s a hint: You’re one of them! Humans have incisors, canines, and molars. Some animals have larger teeth than ours. Animals with large incisors eat plants, chewing up hard nuts and seeds. Long canines are for eating meat—and tall molars are for grinding up grass and other leafy plants.
What kind of animals have two incisors that grow out of their mouth, pointing up at the sky? And which mammal has canine teeth that stretch down toward their belly? Come along for the story of how our mouths evolved with the foods we eat, one pair of teeth at a time.
A scientific exploration of what our teeth tell us about our preferred diet, Tooth by Tooth educates readers on what each type of tooth is best suited to do. Written by Sara Levine, illustrated by T.S Spookytooth, and published by Millbrook Press.

In a little house in the very middle of a small Inuit town where winter is always longer than summer, a little girl named Nalvana lives with her mother. Everywhere she goes, she wears her superhero outfit: a yellow blanket-cape and snowmobiling goggles. Nalvana doesn’t know what her superpower is yet—but she’s determined to find out what it is.
As she goes to school and plays with other kids, Nalvana discovers that many of her friends have superpowers. But Nalvana still hasn’t discovered one of her own. Is it possible Nalvana doesn’t have a superpower? Or is her superpower hidden in plain sight?
What’s My Superpower is a celebration of those who use their words and abilities to lift up the world around them. Filled with references to Inuit language and culture, the narrative focuses on themes of positivity, community, and embracing the things that make us who we are. Written by Aviaq Johnston, illustrated by Tim Mack, and published by Inhabit Media Inc.

Vooks brings children’s storybooks to life through animation. Vooks combines the love, trust, and safety of children’s books with the convenience of online streaming, for a whole new way to experience stories.

What is Vooks?
Vooks brings children’s storybooks to life through animation. With an expansive library of titles, the Vooks storybooks experience feature animation, sound, and narration to classic and award-winning books that are loved by parents and educators alike. Our kid-safe and ad-free streaming library of read-aloud animated storybooks transforms reading by bringing words to life in order to spark every child's imagination. Vooks combines the love, trust, and safety of children’s books with the convenience of online streaming, for a whole new way to experience stories.

From Abraham Lincoln to Rosa Parks, Courageous People Who Changed the World is a perfect introduction to historical figures who stood up to make a difference in the world. Featured are William Wilberforce, Harriet Tubman, Abraham Lincoln, Susan B. Anthony, Mahatma Gandhi, Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King Jr., and Malala Yousafzai. Each story will inspire courage, determination, and a belief that anyone can change the world.
Courageous People Who Changed the World is written by Heidi Poelman, illustrated by Kyle Kershner and published by Familius.

description:
Try Storyteller today: https://bit.ly/40xZxZZ

What is Vooks Storyteller?
Storyteller lets you become the narrator of your favorite Vooks stories so you can share the power of your voice. You don’t have to be a professional narrator… you just have to be you! Because it’s you they love, and it's your voice they will love to hear!

Storyteller allows grandparents, military families, and long-distance relatives to bridge the gaps of time and place and share the bonding experience of storytime with the kids in their lives. It’s also ideal for kids who want to become a part of their favorite stories, teachers who want to track and measure literacy learning or create a sweet, custom gift for their students to give to parents, English Language Learners (or people who are learning Spanish or Hindi), speech-language pathologists, and so much more. It also makes the perfect keepsake gift!

What is Vooks?
Vooks brings children’s storybooks to life through animation. With an expansive library of titles, the Vooks storybooks experience feature animation, sound, and narration to classic and award-winning books that are loved by parents and educators alike. Our kid-safe and ad-free streaming library of read-aloud animated storybooks transforms reading by bringing words to life in order to spark every child's imagination. Vooks combines the love, trust, and safety of children’s books with the convenience of online streaming, for a whole new way to experience stories.

Mozzie the mosquito lives near a pond, down in the meadow. The most beautiful butterflies flutter there all day long. And everyone adores the butterflies—Mozzie most of all. One day, Mozzie builds up her courage, takes a deep breath, and approaches the butterflies. “Can I flutter around with you?” she asks.
But the butterflies don’t hang out with mosquitos, they say. They only like to be around other butterflies, who look and act like they do. So Mozzie came up with a plan—a plan to become a butterfly herself. But when the unexpected happens, being a butterfly might not be so great. Mozzie might need to simply embrace who she’s been all along.
An inversion of the classic Ugly Duckling narrative, The Mozzie with a Sharp Snozzie is a sweet, non-threatening story about self-confidence, bullying, and feeling comfortable in one’s own skin. It also touches on the nature of true friendship and acceptance. Written and illustrated by Irina Goundortseva. Published by Big Sky Publishing.

Mozzie the mosquito lives near a pond, down in the meadow. The most beautiful butterflies flutter there all day long. And everyone adores the butterflies—Mozzie most of all. One day, Mozzie builds up her courage, takes a deep breath, and approaches the butterflies. “Can I flutter around with you?” she asks.
But the butterflies don’t hang out with mosquitos, they say. They only like to be around other butterflies, who look and act like they do. So Mozzie came up with a plan—a plan to become a butterfly herself. But when the unexpected happens, being a butterfly might not be so great. Mozzie might need to simply embrace who she’s been all along.
An inversion of the classic Ugly Duckling narrative, The Mozzie with a Sharp Snozzie is a sweet, non-threatening story about self-confidence, bullying, and feeling comfortable in one’s own skin. It also touches on the nature of true friendship and acceptance. Written and illustrated by Irina Goundortseva. Published by Big Sky Publishing.

Today, Mike and his sister Pam are going on a shopping trip with Daddy. They all pile into the car and head downtown. First, they get haircuts. Mike hops into the chair, and then Pam. Next, they head over to the shoe store. A man measures Mike’s feet, and then he measures Pam’s. Mike picks out blue shoes. Pam is a copycat and picks out blue shoes as well.

The shoe store clerk gives them each a balloon, and Pam picks the same color as Mike. But on the way to the car, Pam’s balloon pops. Daddy gives Pam his balloon—and then decides to make an unexpected stop. Can you guess where they go?

Shopping with Daddy gives young readers a simple overview of a shopping trip—to the barber, a store, and a restaurant. Themes of sharing, copying, and mild sibling rivalry show up throughout the narrative. Written by Harriet Ziefert, illustrated by Travis Foster, and published by Blue Apple Books.

When two fuzzy creatures build a sandcastle on the beach, they agree that it’s pretty much perfect. But then two new friends show up—and they see some room for improvement. It needs a bigger wall. And then a wider foundation. More friends arrive with more suggestions. The castle could also use more towers, and arches, and (of course) windows. And what about a gatehouse and stairs? And a drawbridge—and a moat?

The whole crew decides to work together to make this sandcastle the absolutely most perfect sandcastle ever. But will it actually be perfect? Or will the entire project turn out quite a bit different than anyone expects?

It Is (Not) Perfect deftly explores how trying to change yourself to please others can end in disaster—while also showing how collaboration and a shared vision can bring friends together. Written by Anna Kang and illustrated by Christopher Weyant, It Is (Not) Perfect brings back the endearing characters from the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award winner You Are (Not) Small. Of all the children that ever could be, you are the one made just for me. From a child's first uttered "Dada" to his or her first unsteady steps, nothing can adequately convey the joy and awe of watching the birth and growth of a new child. When two fuzzy creatures build a sandcastle on the beach, they agree that it’s pretty much perfect. But then two new friends show up—and they see some room for improvement. It needs a bigger wall. And then a wider foundation. More friends arrive with more suggestions. The castle could also use more towers, and arches, and (of course) windows. And what about a gatehouse and stairs? And a drawbridge—and a moat?

The whole crew decides to work together to make this sandcastle the absolutely most perfect sandcastle ever. But will it actually be perfect? Or will the entire project turn out quite a bit different than anyone expects?

It Is (Not) Perfect deftly explores how trying to change yourself to please others can end in disaster—while also showing how collaboration and a shared vision can bring friends together. Written by Anna Kang and illustrated by Christopher Weyant, It Is (Not) Perfect brings back the endearing characters from the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award winner You Are (Not) Small. This gentle and calming book is filled with fun firefly facts and a rhyming, rhythmic story.

Jadav lives on an island in the middle of a river. When floodwaters begin destroying the island’s trees, Jadav starts planting bamboo. The shoots grow into a thicket—but Jadav fears it’s not enough. He collects supplies and seeds from neighboring villages. He tends the plants each day. And slowly, acre by acre, animal by animal, the thicket grows into something remarkable. Follow the true-life story of Jadav, the boy who grew a forest. His 1,300-acre sanctuary—that’s over 900 football fields of forest—stands as an important reminder of a powerful truth: A single person can make an incredible difference. The Boy Who Grew a Forest traces the story of Jadav Payeng, a Mishing tribesman whose life demonstrates the importance of personal responsibility, patience, care, and hard work.

Jadav lives on an island in the middle of a river. When floodwaters begin destroying the island’s trees, Jadav starts planting bamboo. The shoots grow into a thicket—but Jadav fears it’s not enough. He collects supplies and seeds from neighboring villages. He tends the plants each day. And slowly, acre by acre, animal by animal, the thicket grows into something remarkable. Follow the true-life story of Jadav, the boy who grew a forest. His 1,300-acre sanctuary—that’s over 900 football fields of forest—stands as an important reminder of a powerful truth: A single person can make an incredible difference. The Boy Who Grew a Forest traces the story of Jadav Payeng, a Mishing tribesman whose life demonstrates the importance of personal responsibility, patience, care, and hard work.

description:
Charlie is tired of being a small bird. He’s tired of being scared, and he’s tired of wishing he was someone else. He longs to be big. So, he sets off to learn the “big” secret from every large animal he can find. First is Moose. Perching on Moose’s antlers makes Charlie feel big—but when Moose runs fast, Charlie can’t hold on. Next, Charlie meets Fish. Fish is big, but only because his pond is so small.
Eventually, Charlie meets Dog. Dog has an idea of how Charlie can be big. But to do as Dog suggests, Charlie will have to be very brave and fly very high. What will happen when Charlie reaches for the sky? Let’s find out.

Today is the perfect day to hike up to Pancake Peak. The air is fresh, Julia is prepared, and she’ll be traveling by herself—just the way she likes it. She plans to trek past Muffin Meadow, through Black Coffee Cave, across Bacon Bridge, over Hashbrown Hill, and finally to the tip-top of Pancake Peak. By the time she gets home, she’ll be just in time for a tasty dinner.
However, Julia doesn’t realize that someone will be following her hike. And atop Pancake Peak, she might pick up a few extra travelers with no way of getting back down. Will Julia’s solo journey be ruined? Or will these tagalongs turn out to be some of her new best friends?
A Vooks Original, The Tagalongs touches on themes of independence, self-reliance, and getting out to enjoy the natural world. The narrative also shows the value of diverse strengths, helping strangers, sharing what we have, and including others—even if we didn’t start out on the same team. Written and illustrated by Megan Marie Myers.

But be careful—the color might get unclogged faster than expected! Little ones will have a blast with this interactive story as they learn primary colors in a whole new way! They’ll also discover how mixing colors makes new colors…and why you should never, ever, put too much trust in a narrator.

What is Vooks?
Vooks is the world’s first streaming platform that brings children’s storybooks to life through animation. With an expansive library of titles, the Vooks storybooks experience feature slight animation, sound, and narration to classic and award-winning books that are loved by parents and educators alike. Our kid-safe and ad-free streaming library of read-aloud animated storybooks transforms reading by bringing words to life in order to spark every child's imagination. Vooks combines the love, trust, and safety of children’s books with the convenience of online streaming, for a whole new way to experience stories. Today is the perfect day to hike up to Pancake Peak. The air is fresh, Julia is prepared, and she’ll be traveling by herself—just the way she likes it. She plans to trek past Muffin Meadow, through Black Coffee Cave, across Bacon Bridge, over Hashbrown Hill, and finally to the tip-top of Pancake Peak. By the time she gets home, she’ll be just in time for a tasty dinner.
However, Julia doesn’t realize that someone will be following her hike. And atop Pancake Peak, she might pick up a few extra travelers with no way of getting back down. Will Julia’s solo journey be ruined? Or will these tagalongs turn out to be some of her new best friends?
A Vooks Original, The Tagalongs touches on themes of independence, self-reliance, and getting out to enjoy the natural world. The narrative also shows the value of diverse strengths, helping strangers, sharing what we have, and including others—even if we didn’t start out on the same team. Written and illustrated by Megan Marie Myers.

Some shapes roll, some don't. Some shapes stack, others won't. Some shapes lie down, while others stand tall. How many shapes are there in all? Circles, squares, and triangles, even ovals, and diamonds. Some shapes we only see at night, glimmering up above. Some shapes tell us where to go. Others make us think of love.
Come along for a journey that’ll make you see shapes—and the world around us—in a totally different way. Because every shape is different, and we’re all made of those shapes. That’s a part of what makes us all the same—and incredibly unique!
Shapes That Roll sees the world through angles, lines, and curves. By connecting the dots of how shapes convey meaning and utility, the narrative teaches new shapes (such as ovals and octagons) while prompting discussion about what a shape represents. Rhythmically written by Karen Nagel and illustrated by Steve Wilson, Shapes That Roll is published by Blue Apple Books.

Some shapes roll, some don't. Some shapes stack, others won't. Some shapes lie down, while others stand tall. How many shapes are there in all? Circles, squares, and triangles, even ovals, and diamonds. Some shapes we only see at night, glimmering up above. Some shapes tell us where to go. Others make us think of love.
Come along for a journey that’ll make you see shapes—and the world around us—in a totally different way. Because every shape is different, and we’re all made of those shapes. That’s a part of what makes us all the same—and incredibly unique!
Shapes That Roll sees the world through angles, lines, and curves. By connecting the dots of how shapes convey meaning and utility, the narrative teaches new shapes (such as ovals and octagons) while prompting discussion about what a shape represents. Rhythmically written by Karen Nagel and illustrated by Steve Wilson, Shapes That Roll is published by Blue Apple Books.
